name: Common contract boundary counterexamples
summary: Review-only negative knowledge for similarities that do not establish stronger guarantees.
negative_claim: For the listed interfaces and conditions, a shared storage or coordination shape does not establish the stronger guarantee named by the target concept.

counterexamples.description: An append-only log can still permit deletion, compaction, or retention-based loss.
counterexamples.implication: Append-only must not be upgraded to immutable without evidence about retention and deletion semantics.

counterexamples.description: Replicas may copy state without agreeing on a single ordered decision under faults.
counterexamples.implication: Replication alone does not justify a consensus or linearizability claim.

counterexamples.description: A point-in-time snapshot can coexist with writes that violate transaction isolation guarantees.
counterexamples.implication: Snapshot semantics must not be treated as proof of transaction isolation.

counterexamples.description: A reconciliation procedure can terminate while unresolved conflicts or non-idempotent rules remain.
counterexamples.implication: Reconciliation is not a convergence proof without stated laws and checked outcomes.

evidence.title: Mathen contract boundary review
evidence.notes: Representative bounded implications; not a universal theorem.
